newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty focus on dlr/mark, currency-selling fades.
newsitem.headline: Zloty focus on dlr/mark, currency-selling fades.

text.p: The Polish zloty narrowed in on 2.4 percent from the parity rate in early Wednesday trade as the market's months-old pro-zloty sentiment took a back seat to dollar/mark moves on world markets, dealers said.

"The zloty is in tune with dollar/mark moves and the market's currency-selling sentiment may have faded with (dollar) buying more prominent during the last few days," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
Dealers said however the zloty may move toward resistance levels at 2.5 percent from parity later today as banks cut currency exposure, taking advantage of Friday's value date.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was at 2.41/2.37 percent from the central parity rate against the opening 2.44/2.33 percent and Tuesday's close at 2.44/2.49 percent.
It was at 3.1435/50 to the dollar and at 1.8605/10 to the mark, against opening levels of 3.1370/00 and 1.8635/55.

Dealers said that after weeks of battling with central bank interventions whenever the zloty gained past resistance, the market's bullish zloty sentiment may be starting to change as foreign entry into Polish treasuries slows.
One-day rates held steady around 22 percent as the market remained liquid despite today's cash outflow and the central bank's 300 million zloty reverse repo announcement.
Overnight rates were quoted around 21.75/22.10 percent in morning trade, unchanged from opening. Tomorrow/next rates inched up 0.05 point to 21.90/22.15 percent.
